discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 300658
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
258 AM EDT Fri Oct 30 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Patchy dense fog early this morning.

- Not as warm today through the weekend with highs in the low-
  to-mid 60s.

- Plenty of dry time on Halloween, but there is a 20-30% chance
  of rain showers west of I-69.

- Periods of rain next week and very mild on Tuesday.
  

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 258 AM EDT Fri Oct 30 2026

High pressure seeps in today in the wake of yesterday's cold front. 
Light northwesterly flow after sunset prompted areas of lake-
enhanced fog generally along and west of US 31, with patchy 
instances of dense fog as far east as Huntington and Marion. Overall 
this fog has been rather transient, with observations bouncing 
around except in a couple pesky locations. Water vapor depicts 
a mid- level trough axis now exiting MI which should prompt 
northeast flow to bring drier air into the region over these 
next few hours, working to mix out locally dense fog.

Falling shy of a record high temperature by 1 degree at Fort 
Wayne yesterday, today will be cooler with highs only in the 
low-to-mid 60s area-wide (yet normal for this date is 57). 
Temperatures of this magnitude are in store for much of the 
forecast period with the exception of Tuesday and Wednesday when
70s return thanks to robust warm air advection ahead of a mid 
latitude cyclone. But first, a weak warm front attempts to lifts
into the mid-Missippi valley Saturday morning bringing a 20-30%
chance of isolated rain showers to areas west of I-69. Plenty 
of dry hours on Halloween but rather cloudy with high 
temperatures generally near 60.

Rain chances become more widespread next week starting with a 
trough passing through the Ohio valley Sunday afternoon and 
evening (20-30% chance for now, with the trough's track still in
flux). The primary system we've been monitoring spills onshore 
of the West Coast this weekend, arriving to our doorstep 
Tuesday/Wednesday. Low pressure emerges in the Lee of the 
Rockies as a deep trough pushes inland. A surface low wraps up 
over the Northern Plains, occludes, prompting renewed 
cyclogenesis of the Central Plains. This spells a period of 
mild and breezy conditions locally on Tuesday and Wednesday as 
the upper-level pattern becomes highly amplified over the 
eastern Great Lakes. A period of steady rain is probable 
Wednesday as this system moves through. At this distance, any 
severe weather risk appears to lie elsewhere owing to a 
distinct lack of instability. Wet weather may linger into the 
end of the week depending on how the low wraps up over the 
eastern CONUS. No significant cool-downs noted in its wake. &&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z SATURDAY/...
Issued at 1249 AM EDT Fri Oct 30 2026

A cold front has now exited the area which ultimately prompted a
brief period of marine-enhanced fog. This area of fog appears to
be drifting SSE based on satellite and surface observations.
Medium-high confidence this marine-modified air mass will
bypass KFWA. Flow veers to become NNE later this morning which 
will disrupt the modified air mass. Otherwise today, increasing 
high clouds as a disorganized area of low pressure lifts into 
the Midwest. Rain is possible at KSBN just beyond this TAF 
period.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

spc.text:
SPC AC 301619

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1119 AM CDT Fri Oct 30 2026

   Valid 301630Z - 311200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR THE MIDDLE
   COAST OF TEXAS AND CENTRAL INTO SOUTHERN ARIZONA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   An isolated risk for severe weather is possible today along the
   middle coast of Texas and central into southern Arizona.

   ...Middle Coast of TX...
   An upper trough and associated vorticity maximum evident in midday
   water-vapor imagery over the Rio Grande Valley will continue
   east-northeast and reach the Ark-La-Tex and northwest Gulf Coast by
   late evening.  A zone of warm advection immediately ahead of the
   disturbance will advance northeast up the coast during the
   afternoon.  The inland penetration of higher theta-e into the
   coastal counties may result in sufficient buoyancy for a couple of
   stronger updrafts.  Some enlargement of the low-level portion of the
   hodograph within a moist environment may yield a risk for a brief
   tornado near the coast this afternoon.  

   ...Arizona...
   A shortwave trough moving into southern CA will continue northeast
   towards the Four Corners during the period.  Copious mid to
   high-level cloud cover will likely limit heating of a seasonably
   moist boundary layer across the lower desert.  Model guidance
   continues to indicate the possibility for a few stronger
   thunderstorms developing later today.  An isolated risk for
   marginally severe hail and localized severe gusts may accompany the
   stronger thunderstorms.

   ..Smith/Chalmers.. 10/30/2026

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 300540

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1240 AM CDT Fri Oct 30 2026

   Valid 311200Z - 011200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not expected on Saturday.

   ...Discussion...
   Shortwave ridging will occur from the Northern Plains to the Upper
   Great Lakes on Saturday as a shortwave trough exits the Maritimes
   and multiple waves converge across the West. In the wake of the
   northeastern trough, high pressure will become centered over the Mid
   Atlantic, with dry low-level trajectories over much of the eastern
   CONUS. 

   Easterly surface winds will maintain a boundary near the Gulf Coast,
   though southerly winds may bring upper 60s well inland across
   eastern TX into LA. Here, scattered showers and thunderstorms will
   be likely within a weak low-level warm advection regime. Lapse rates
   will be poor with little if any severe potential.

   Elsewhere, cool temperatures aloft will exist along the West Coast
   and into much of the Intermountain West as an amplified upper trough
   moves ashore late in the day over WA/OR/CA, and another
   southern-stream wave approaches southern CA and northern Baja
   overnight. While shear will increase across most of the region,
   instability will be quite weak, with isolated lightning possible
   from eastern ID southward across the Great Basin late in the day and
   overnight.

   ..Jewell.. 10/30/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 300730

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0230 AM CDT Fri Oct 30 2026

   Valid 011200Z - 021200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER MUCH OF
   CENTRAL AND EASTERN NEW MEXICO...AND SMALL PARTS OF WESTERN TEXAS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   A few severe storms are anticipated from central New Mexico into
   parts of western Texas late Sunday into Sunday night.

   ...Discussion...
   An amplified upper trough will move across the Great Basin on
   Sunday, while another wave to the south moves across northern Baja
   CA and into AZ. By late in the day, gusty south winds will increase
   across the Rockies and into the southern High Plains, as low
   pressure develops over WY through 00Z.

   During the late evening and overnight, a prominent cold front will
   move out of AZ and into NM as the parent wave aloft continues
   northeastward across NM and into the central to southern High
   Plains. The surface low is forecast to deepen overnight into CO,
   with a surface trough into eastern NM and western TX through 12Z
   Monday.

   After a full day of heating, low-level lapse rates will be steep,
   and gusty winds overnight should maintain relatively warm
   temperatures ahead of the cold front. Dewpoints from the upper 40s
   to mid 50s F should also be maintained ahead of the front, with
   thunderstorms developing near the cold front after about 03-06Z.
   Deep-layer shear will be strong, with supercell wind profiles.
   Instability will be marginal over central NM, perhaps supporting
   locally severe gusts or marginal hail, with a potentially greater
   concentration of severe storms into eastern NM where low-level
   moisture will be more abundant with MUCAPE over 1000 J/kg. The
   strongest cooling aloft will spread over northern NM and into the TX
   Panhandle, and this is where a potentially greater hail and wind
   threat could develop. Both cellular and possibly QLCS storm mode
   will be possible, with storms tied to the cold front. A small
   corridor of higher severe probabilities could be added in later
   outlooks as trends warrant.

   ..Jewell.. 10/30/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
